method: Mapped every store whose RIP-relative target lands anywhere in 0x4213c0..0x421500, then projected the targets onto a byte grid to see which slots are never written.

interpretation.fact: Almost every slot in the region has an identified writer; exactly five 8-byte slots never receive a direct store: 0x4213c0, 0x4213e8, 0x421418, 0x421420 and 0x421428.
interpretation.getters: Two of those five, 0x4213c0 and 0x4213e8, are the targets of the only two address-of getters in the module that reach this region, and both are only touched by an or-based link stub rather than by a store.
interpretation.grouping: The three remaining untouched slots, 0x421418, 0x421420 and 0x421428, are consecutive and sit at 0x4213e8 + 0x30, +0x38 and +0x40, so they read as fields of the object at 0x4213e8.
interpretation.consequence: The object at 0x4213e8 is therefore constructed or copied as a whole by code that never stores to those offsets directly, which is consistent with a constructor that receives the object address in a register or with a bulk copy, and with the field holding a live heap pointer at run time.

adjacent_writers_explained: 0x3a530 and 0x3a600 are the lazy-create and destroy pair for a different singleton (0x4213d8 / 0x4213e0): new 0x18, vtables 0x33d398 and 0x348880, then new 0x28 stored at +0x10. They do not touch the object at 0x4213e8.
boundary: Routes A and B, the getter-indirection follow-up and the cross-module check are all complete and all negative. The publisher of 0x421428 is not visible as a direct store anywhere in the static image of the three modules.
not_claimed: that no publisher exists in these modules under any encoding
that the object at 0x4213e8 is identified by name
